lines.text: own motion, voluntarily. परितापाय—mark the sense of परि; they
trouble in every way. शमसुखम्—शम is the same as शान्ति; comp.
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः । निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शान्तिमधि-
गच्छति ॥ Bg. II. 71; also 70, 72. It is not used in its technical
Vedántic sense here ( for which see Mis. sl. 2. )
Sl. 14. ब्रह्म &c.-those who possess विवेक discrimination
(between what is real and what is unreal) from their knowledge
of Brahman. एकान्ततो निःस्पृहाः—absolutely free from all desires.
न च प्राप्तौ दृढप्रत्ययः—(we have) no firm belief in their attainment;
we are not sure that they would be attained. वाञ्छामात्र &c.—
Although they ( enjoyments ) are seized only by desire ( i. e. by
imagination ); although their possession is only imaginary.
Sl. 15. शकुनाः—birds. अहेहेमयाः:-an aluk comp. मनोरथ &c.—
for the different ways of dissolving the comp., see com. मनो-
रथोप०—a palace built in the mind &c ; i. e. building castles in
the air.

r4.note: The Sanskrit compound in line 1 and abbreviation in line 3 are unclear.

lines.text: Sl. 16. भिक्षाशनं-भिक्षया अशनं livelihood; or भिक्ष्यते इति भिक्षा (food
obtained by begging), fr. भिक्ष् + अ; तस्या अशनं eating, maintenance
on. तदपि—also goes with एकवारं, even the coarse food is
to be had for but one meal; it is not sufficient for the two
meals in the day. न जहाति—In spite of abject poverty
attachment to worldly objects does not die out. विषया
न परित्यजन्ति v. l.—in this case some such word as अस्मान्
must be supplied. But this reading loses force since there is no
beauty in saying that the pleasures do not leave us. It is the
mind that must relinquish them. Hence the reading adopted
in the text is preferable.

r5.note: Some Sanskrit text in the first three lines is indistinct.

lines.text: Sl. 17. कविजनविशेषैः—by particular poets. गुरुकृतम्—ma-
gnified, praised, made much of.

r6.note: The Sanskrit words are somewhat indistinct.

lines.text: Sl. 18. रागिन्—one in the power of love, an amorous person.
प्रियतमा०—S'iva and Párvati form together but one body the
right half being male and the left one being female. Cf. ‘देह-
द्वयार्धघटितं शरीरमेकं ययोः &c.’ Intro. s'lokas to Kád. Pt. II.

r7.note: The Sanskrit quotation and abbreviated word are indistinct.
